runs.question: Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
runs.answer:
[Turn 1 | session=ses_0eecae342ffe2XGwf96Dl9nMll] Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
Here are the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 UTC. The query returned **7180 blocks** across the day, showing per-block the earliest time any sentry node observed each block (in milliseconds after slot start).

**Columns:** `slot`, `slot_start_date_time`, `block_root`, `first_seen_ms`

**Sample rows:**

| slot | slot_start_date_time | first_seen_ms |
|------|---------------------|--------------|
| 14590518 | 2026-06-20 00:00:11 | 1264 |
| 14590519 | 2026-06-20 00:00:23 | 1465 |
| 14590520 | 2026-06-20 00:00:35 | 1267 |
| ... | ... | ... |
| 14597698 | 2026-06-20 22:59:59 | 1626 |
| 14597998 | 2026-06-20 23:59:59 | 1329 |

The `first_seen_ms` values (MIN of `seen_slot_start_diff` across all observing nodes) range roughly from **~215 ms** (fastest arrivals, e.g. slot 14597916 at 215ms) to **~3700 ms** (slowest). Most blocks were first seen within **1200–1800 ms** of slot start. Some slots show notably fast propagation (e.g. 224ms, 232ms, 491ms, 522ms, 703ms).

[Turn 2 | session=ses_0eecae342ffe2XGwf96Dl9nMll] Plot the distribution of those arrival times as a chart.
Here's the distribution of first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026:

![](http://127.0.0.1:2480/api/v1/storage/files/df1c78753783/70c34b0c-1fe8-4a5e-9771-1fa9c3c18247/block_arrival_distribution.png)

**Chart:** `block_arrival_distribution.png`  
**Finding:** Mainnet block arrival times cluster around **1.2–1.4 seconds** after slot start, with the bulk falling between ~1.0s and ~1.8s. A long tail extends to ~3.5s+, representing slower-propagating blocks. The chart is based on 7,180 mainnet blocks observed on 20 June 2026, showing the minimum `seen_slot_start_diff` (in ms) per block across all sentry nodes.
